assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from proglucagon-derived peptide biology and the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) to long-acting agonists, has produced a new class of therapy for type 2 diabetes and obesity with large outcome benefits. The mechanistic arc and clinical transformation are exceptionally clear.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst are the clearest physiological contributors (incretin biology, GLP-1 action, intestinal trophic effects). Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 form is a credible third claim, but priority relative to other early groups is contested. Knudsen's drug-development role is real but more industrial; I would not include her in a three-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, multiple approved drugs, cardiovascular and renal outcome trials; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Mojsov priority and patent-related credit disputes are not resolved by the supplied text.
Whether the committee prefers to recognise the physiology or the engineered drugs (Knudsen) is open.
Other early contributors (e.g. Habener) are not on the credited list, which limits the fairness of the configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed at tumour antigens have created a new modality in oncology, with durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukaemias and lymphomas and now expanding to myeloma and autoimmune settings. Conceptually original and clinically transformative.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CD28 costimulated CARs and early design logic) and June (clinical translation, CD19 41BB CAR, first durable remissions) are central; Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer and TIL work established the broader concept and early gene-engineered T-cell trials. The original chimeric-receptor concept (Eshhar) is not among the credited names, which is a fairness concern.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and a decade of follow-up; toxicity, solid-tumour limitations and access remain, but the core principle is firmly established.
uncertainties: Omission of the original CAR concept originator from the credited names complicates attribution.
Allocation between design (Sadelain) and clinical proof (June) versus the earlier cell therapy field (Rosenberg) is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics transformed neuroscience by enabling causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity with millisecond precision. Channelrhodopsin discovery plus its deployment in neurons underpin a vast body of circuit research, and some clinical vision-restoration applications are emerging.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) identified and characterised channelrhodopsins; Deisseroth (and Boyden) demonstrated neuronal control and built the toolkit. Six credited names exceed the three-laureate limit, so the configuration is difficult and Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck have strong claims. My picks balance the molecular discovery and the neuroscience implementation but exclude deserving people.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and replicated across thousands of laboratories; impact is lasting and mature, though therapeutic payoff is still limited.
uncertainties: Dispute over who most deserves the neuronal-application credit (Deisseroth vs Boyden vs Miesenböck).
Whether a tool/method fits the Physiology or Medicine criteria as strongly as a discovery with medical benefit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defines how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, with relevance to infection, autoimmunity (interferonopathies), cancer immunity and ageing. A clear mechanistic discovery with second messenger cGAMP as a novel signalling principle.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP as the second messenger; Barber discovered STING. Together they cover the sensor and the adaptor, forming a clean two-person configuration. Other credited names (Ishikawa, Sun, Wu) were primarily trainee or co-discovery contributors and I would not add them.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed mechanistically; therapeutic translation (STING agonists and antagonists) is still not clinically proven, so recognition rests on basic discovery, which is acceptable but a little earlier than ideal.
uncertainties: STING agonist and inhibitor clinical efficacy remains unproven.
Allocation of credit for related work on cyclic dinucleotide sensing (not among the credited names) is not covered.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR identification as the central controller of cell growth and nutrient response is a foundational discovery in cell physiology with relevance to cancer, metabolism, ageing, immunology and transplantation, with rapalogs in clinical use.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically in yeast and established its role as a growth regulator; Sabatini defined mammalian mTORC1/2 regulation and nutrient sensing. Schreiber's work on rapamycin-FKBP12 chemical biology was important but arguably more tool-defining; the original rapamycin drug discovery (Sehgal and others) is outside the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature with decades of independent confirmation across species, though some trust issues around Sabatini's later history may affect committee appetite.
uncertainties: Controversy affecting one possible laureate could influence deliberation and is not documented in the supplied text.
Rapamycin discovery credit lies partly outside the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed how cells monitor ER protein folding load and signal to the nucleus, a paradigm of intracellular signalling with implications for secretory disease, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently elucidated IRE1-Hac1/XBP1 signalling and the first intracellular stress pathway from the ER to the nucleus. Clear and compact two-person attribution, though Walter's and Mori's complementary roles overlap with others (e.g. Ron on PERK/ATF4) not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Mature and extensively confirmed; Lasker recognition already given. Clinical translation is still developing (ISRIB, UPR modulators in neurodegeneration), which weakens the medical-benefit element.
uncertainties: Contributions of the PERK/ATF6 branches and other contributors are not represented in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) turned a lethal infant neurological disease into a treatable one and established a template for splice-modulating therapeutics. Strong translational impact with clear mechanistic origin.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing-regulatory mechanism and the ASO target; Bennett led the oligonucleotide chemistry and drug development. The two-person configuration is clean, but others (e.g. Hua, Singh, Rigo) contributed and are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Approved in 2016 with years of real-world follow-up; the mechanism is well confirmed, although the field is relatively young and may have only just become mature enough for the highest recognition.
uncertainties: Foundational contributions to SMN gene identification and to antisense chemistry broaden the credit question.
Whether a drug-development story is preferred over the underlying mechanistic discovery is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of Wnt (Int-1) and the Wnt signalling pathway links oncogene biology to developmental patterning and stem-cell renewal, and is a pillar of cell signalling in development and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Nusse and Varmus identified Int-1 as an MMTV-activated proto-oncogene and Nusse then built the Wnt field; Varmus already holds a Nobel Prize (retroviral oncogenes), which may reduce the case for a second award. Wnt pathway elucidation involved many others (Wieschaus/Nüsslein-Volhard on wingless already recognised), so a fair configuration is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and broadly confirmed, but therapeutic translation (Wnt-directed drugs) has been disappointing and the discovery has partly been recognised through the Drosophila patterning prize.
uncertainties: Varmus's earlier Nobel Prize weighs against including him.
Overlap with the 1995 recognition of Drosophila developmental genes complicates the claim for novelty.
